_note: Read by tools/calibration_report.py for the report's 'What changed' section. Each entry names the parameters it changed as [from, to] (from null: a new parameter); the script checks each parameter's latest 'to' against core/data/table_params.json and lists any that no longer match. Update it with every tuning.
heading: What changed from the starting values: M1's tuning to the published sources, then the owner's feel sessions

changes.why: refitted by least squares to the published half-ball stun throw (Alciatore, Billiards Digest Sept 2006; Jewett 1995). The old fit threw 1.7 degrees on a firm cut against 3.45 measured.
Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin's measurements on a snooker table and ball (Am. J. Phys. 2009; Proc. IMechE 2010), the same source as the cushion model.
the fast end of the snooker evidence that the lag target allows (Mathavan measured 0.0127 on an unheated lab table).
pooltool's snooker cue (ball mass / 30): squirt at maximum side drops from 3.05 to 2.0 degrees, inside C9's 1-3.
the slope is a least-squares fit to Mathavan's measured rebounds above 2.5 m/s (Proc. IMechE 2010, Fig. 7b); the floor is Alciatore's typical rail restitution (TP B.6).

changes.what: The cloth's pace, by the owner's feel
changes.why: KaiC's feel sessions on the iPhone, 2026-11-13 to 15, tuned live over the phone link. Slower than the published fast-cloth range the lag target (C11) was built from, and a little slower than the one snooker measurement (0.0127); C11 now holds the lag to his table and shows the published range beside it.

changes.what: The cushions' bounce, by the owner's feel
changes.why: the same sessions. Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin fitted 0.98 to their measured rebounds; with 0.85 a ball rolling straight in keeps 80% of its speed instead of 91%, and hard hits reach the 0.7 floor at 3.4 m/s into the cushion instead of 4.25. C7 and C8 check the model at his value; the paper's rebounds stay in the cushion reference and are checked with the paper's value.
